Was/Were Going To for Unfulfilled Events
When we want to talk about plans that we made, but didn't happen, we can use be going to in the past.
Use was/were going to when talking about events that were planned, but actually did not happened.
I was going to download something I had on my cloud storage service, but I couldn't because it was out of service I guess.
In the past, if you were going to claim for losses because of a cloud outage, this claim wouldn't fit into the insured's policies.
Subject + was / were + going to + base form of the verb

Examples:
I was going to do some research on insurance plans for cloud services, but I didn't find much information about it.
I was going to ask for cloud computing services protection, but the insurer told me they didn't offer specific policies for my needs.
Things That Can Go Wrong in Cloud Computing
As in any computing service, many things can go wrong in cloud services. Here, we list the most common issues:

• Interruption of service because of a cloud outage.
  • Interruption of services because of a programmed maintenance.
  • User erasing data by mistake.
  • User being unable to access data from a non-predetermined location.
  • Loss of data due to a cloud disaster and data recovery is unsuccessful.
  • Loss of data due to lack of back up.
  • Cloud serves being hacked into and data being stolen.
  • Contract agreement disputes in which data gets locked in.
  • Cloud provider going down permanently.

images.text:
Professor: Nowadays, cloud services are becoming increasingly popular in businesses due to the massive cost savings in hardware. There are, however, many things that can go wrong with cloud computing services. Sarah, can you mention some of them?
Sarah: Of course. I believe the most common one is the interruption of service because of a cloud outage. It once happened to me. I was going to download something I had on my cloud storage service, but I couldn't because it was out of service I guess. There's also the risk of hacking and getting your data stolen. Another common problem is when there is data loss and the recovery tools are not adequate. Actually, I was going to ask you about that. Is there any insurance coverage on data loss or theft?

Professor: Insurers, cloud providers and cloud users are now starting to realize how important it is to have clearer terms about insurance options. Most cyber insurance policies exclude loss of data in cloud-related events. In the past, if you were going to claim for losses because of a cloud outage, this claim wouldn't fit into the insured's policies.
Sarah: All things considered, I guess insurance companies are now offering cloud-related products, am I right?

Professor: Yes. Some specific cloud insurance policies are now providing coverage against liability claims for data loss and outages. Additionally, they are covering the costs of technical issues, data restoration and back up services due to outages.
Sarah: Is the loss of data due to hacking covered by these new insurance policies?
Professor: Yes. There are emerging products with coverage for loss of income because of an outage and losses incurred for the leakage of sensitive information due to a security breach or hacking.
Sarah: Thanks, professor. You've been enlightening.
